column3: NASB renders “exhort” as “entreat,” “in the Lord” as “of the Lord,” and “worthily” as “in a manner worthy,” and it reorders the verse.
NASB renders “bearing with” as “showing forbearance to.”
NASB renders “keep” as “preserve.”
NASB adds “There is.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text without “you.”
NASB renders “has been given” as “was given.”
The quotation is in capitals; “led captive captivity” is rendered “LED CAPTIVE A HOST OF CAPTIVES.” NASB includes “AND,” which the critical text lacks.
NASB follows the critical text without “first”; it opens a parenthesis, adds “this expression,” and renders “regions” as “parts.”
NASB closes the parenthesis and adds “far.”
NASB renders “shepherds” as “pastors.”
NASB renders “perfecting” as “equipping” and “ministry” as “service.”
NASB renders “a complete man” as “a mature man” and adds “which belongs to.”
NASB renders “infants” as “children” and “cunning” as “trickery,” and it adds “here and there.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “we may grow up” as “we are to grow up” and “in all things” as “in all aspects,” and adds “even.”
NASB restructures the verse, rendering “every ligament of its supply” as “that which every joint supplies.”
NASB follows the critical text without “other”; “testify in the Lord” is rendered “affirm together with the Lord.”
NASB follows the critical text; “alienated” is rendered “excluded.”
NASB renders “having cast off all feeling” as “having become callous.”

Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “old man” as “old self” and “desires” as “lusts.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “new man” as “new self” and “according to God” as “in the likeness of God.”
NASB puts the allusion in capitals and adds “of you.”
NASB puts the allusion in capitals and renders “should not set” as “do not let … go down.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “neither” as “and do not.”
NASB follows the critical text (“his own”); “toil working” is rendered “labor, performing,” and “impart” is “share.”
NASB adds “only such a word” and renders “of the need” as “according to the need of the moment.”
NASB renders “in whom” as “by whom.”
